solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Illegal reproduction of photo largely blue (6)

indicatorNotes.largely: most of the word but not all of it: the last letter goes

blocks.note: blue = risqué, racy, as in a blue joke

annotation.surface: A complaint about someone copying a rather saucy picture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' tempts you toward copying a photo; it is the definition's second word, and the photo is just PIC cut short.
annotation.definitionFit: Piracy is the illegal copying of films, music or software.

entries.clue: Reduction in amount of wine is grating? (10)

blocks.note: a cull reduces numbers, e.g. of a herd

annotation.surface: A wine lover grumbling that cutting their ration is irritating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grating' reads as annoying; the question mark flags that it is a noun here, the iron grille dropped over a castle gateway.
annotation.definitionFit: A portcullis is a heavy lattice grating lowered to block a castle gate.

entries.clue: Greek’s letter to bank not out for money (5)

indicatorNotes.to bank: RHO banks, i.e. keeps safe inside it, the letters IN

blocks.note: the opposite of out, as a batsman still in

annotation.surface: A Greek writing to the bank about money that isn't out of the account.
annotation.walkthrough: RHINO is old British slang for money. The banking surface is misdirection that happens to fit the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhino is a dated British slang word for money.

entries.clue: Large Turner in public gallery ultimately replica? (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the final letter of each of the two words before it

blocks.note: a clone is an exact copy

annotation.surface: Asking whether a big Turner painting on show in a public gallery might be a fake.
annotation.walkthrough: Turner the painter is the misdirection: a Turner here is anything that turns, and a cyclone is a huge rotating storm.
annotation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a large system of winds turning around a centre of low pressure.

entries.clue: Stone breaks pieces of glass instrument (8)

indicatorNotes.breaks: the stone breaks into the panes, sitting inside them

blocks.note: a fruit stone, as in a cherry pip

annotation.surface: A thrown stone shatters a glass instrument.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like vandalism; 'breaks' just means the stone breaks into, i.e. sits inside, PA...NES.
annotation.definitionFit: Panpipes are a wind instrument of joined pipes of different lengths.

entries.clue: Body part from an animal turned up (5)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down entry, 'up' means read bottom to top, so ELK flips

annotation.surface: A body part from some animal has been found.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as discovered; in a down clue it reverses the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: The ankle is the joint between foot and leg.

entries.clue: Trailblazer in seaside attraction eating sole (7)

indicatorNotes.eating: the pier takes ONE inside it

blocks.note: a British seaside pier, a walkway over the sea with amusements

annotation.surface: Someone bold at a seaside pier, tucking into a sole.
annotation.walkthrough: Sole looks like the fish you might eat at the seaside; here it means single, ONE.
annotation.definitionFit: A pioneer is the first to open up new ground, a trailblazer.

entries.clue: Rod smashed cafe mug showing no emotion (5,4)

indicatorNotes.smashed: the letters of CAFE are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: a fire poker is an iron rod

annotation.surface: Someone smashes a cafe mug with a rod and stays completely calm.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like crockery beside 'cafe', but it is slang for face.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom from the card game, where players hide their hand behind a blank expression; mug is slang for the face wearing it.

entries.clue: All there was extra in file, conclusively (4)

indicatorNotes.conclusively: take the concluding letter of each word

annotation.surface: Confirming that nothing is missing and one extra item turned up in a file.
annotation.walkthrough: 'All there' looks like a complete file; it is the idiom for being of sound mind.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone 'all there' is mentally sound, sane.

entries.clue: What will get you half-way from A to B? (8)

annotation.definition: What will get you half-way from A to B?

blocks.note: the surface reads as a journey; the setter means half of a musical step
not two places but two musical notes, a whole tone apart

annotation.surface: A riddle about a journey stopping midway between two places.
annotation.walkthrough: A and B are musical notes a whole tone apart, so half that step is a semitone; the question mark marks the play on travel.
annotation.definitionFit: A semitone is half a tone, the interval between A and B.

entries.clue: Reported means of controlling verification for replacement Superbowl ticket? (9)

indicatorNotes.Reported: said out loud, so REIN is heard as RAIN

annotation.surface: News of new ticket-checking controls at the Super Bowl.
annotation.walkthrough: A rain check is the American ticket given for a game postponed by weather; the question mark admits the Super Bowl is only an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A rain check is a ticket for a replacement fixture when a game is rained off.

entries.clue: Voodoo’s back with a doll made of wood (5)

indicatorNotes.back: the back of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A voodoo doll carved out of wood.
annotation.walkthrough: Voodoo and doll together summon a pin-cushion effigy; the doll is Ken, and voodoo gives only its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain adjective: the -en ending, as in wooden or golden, marks what something is made of, here oak.

entries.clue: I also corrected dodgy artificial eye drops (9,5)

indicatorNotes.dodgy: unreliable, so the letters are not in their right order

annotation.surface: Someone admits fixing some unreliable artificial eye drops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corrected' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'dodgy' does the mixing. Eye drops are tears, and artificial ones are faked.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom for feigned weeping, from the old belief that crocodiles cry while eating; the drops fall from the eye but the grief is fake.

entries.clue: Nag colleague to declare hosting capable maiden? (10)

indicatorNotes.hosting: STATE hosts, holding the other letters inside it

blocks.note: M = maiden, a scoreless over in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: Pestering a coworker to admit she is a competent young woman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nag' looks like a verb meaning pester; it is a horse, and a stablemate is a horse from the same stable.
annotation.definitionFit: A stablemate is a horse sharing a stable, a nag's colleague.

entries.clue: Run out of large part of church (5)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing sizes
the apse is the rounded end of a church

annotation.surface: Someone fleeing from a big section of a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Run out' reads as dashing away; here it means expire, as a subscription lapses.
annotation.definitionFit: A licence or policy that lapses has run out.

entries.clue: Dash to the pass very quickly (9)

indicatorNotes.to: the dash is added to the end of the pass

blocks.note: to post something is to pass it on, as in the mail

annotation.surface: Rushing up to a mountain pass as fast as possible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'X to Y' can mean X added on the end of Y. The pass looks like a mountain route; it is the verb pass on, as letters are sent.
annotation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, very quickly.

entries.clue: Practising hobby regularly with help (9)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take every other letter, here the second and fourth

blocks.note: a servant is a help, as in 'the help'

annotation.surface: Someone keeping up a hobby, practising regularly with assistance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Practising' looks like rehearsal; the sense is religious, as an observant Jew or Catholic keeps the rules.
annotation.definitionFit: An observant believer is one who practises the faith's rules.

entries.clue: Bit of stage scenery in corner, perhaps (3,5)

blocks.note: a free-standing piece of a theatre set
a planned restart in football, a corner kick being one

annotation.surface: A piece of theatre scenery shoved in a corner.
annotation.walkthrough: In football a set piece is a rehearsed restart such as a corner kick; 'perhaps' warns that a corner is only one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A set piece is both a piece of stage set and a planned football restart like a corner.

entries.clue: Broke in to crack den overnight, at last (9)

indicatorNotes.at last: take the last letter of each of the two words before it

annotation.surface: A burglary report: someone forced their way into a crack den during the night.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broke in' is the obvious phrase, but 'Broke' alone is the definition, meaning penniless; 'crack' is solve, not the drug.
annotation.definitionFit: Insolvent means unable to pay debts, broke.

entries.clue: Wasn’t honest to have short rest? (3,4)

annotation.surface: Asking whether fibbing about needing a nap counts as dishonest.
annotation.walkthrough: The split falls after LIED, not LIE; the question mark flags the noun, a lie-down, a brief rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A lie-down is a short rest lying on a bed or sofa.

entries.clue: Nerd drew after losing on buzzer round (5)

indicatorNotes.round: turn BEE round so it reads backwards

blocks.note: DREW minus RE, where re = on, concerning

annotation.surface: A quiz swot's handwriting after being beaten to the buzzer in a round.
annotation.walkthrough: The quiz surface is misdirection: buzzer is an insect and round only turns it around. RE for 'on' means about.
annotation.definitionFit: A dweeb is a boring, studious or socially awkward person, a nerd.

entries.clue: Resentment once golf stops guy working (7)

indicatorNotes.stops: G stops up DUDE, plugging a gap inside it

blocks.note: G = golf in the NATO alphabet
on = working, as a machine switched on

annotation.surface: Bitterness once a golfing round stops a man from working.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like a halt to work; it means plugs, putting G inside DUDE.
annotation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of offended resentment, as in 'in high dudgeon'.

entries.clue: Children bite me for changing nursery rhyme (5,5,4)

annotation.surface: A tired carer complaining that the children bite during a nappy change and nursery rhymes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changing' looks like changing nappies in a nursery; it tells you to rearrange the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Three Blind Mice is a well-known English nursery rhyme.

entries.clue: Spirits possibly live outside madhouse to the north (5)

indicatorNotes.outside: BE goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.to the north: in a down entry, going north means reading upward, so ZOO reverses

blocks.note: a zoo is a chaotic place, a madhouse

annotation.surface: Ghosts that might live near an asylum up north.
annotation.walkthrough: Spirits look like ghosts beside 'madhouse'; they are drinks, and 'possibly' concedes booze covers more than spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: Booze is alcoholic drink, of which spirits are one kind.

entries.clue: Prelude featured in fortnightly retrospective? (5)

indicatorNotes.featured in: the answer's letters are found within the next word
indicatorNotes.retrospective: looking backwards, so the letters read in reverse

annotation.surface: An opening feature in a magazine's twice-monthly look back.
annotation.walkthrough: The magazine surface disguises the device: a retrospective looks back, so the letters are read in reverse.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal clipping of introduction, the opening passage of a song or piece of music.

entries.clue: Eager to leave silver plates (4)

indicatorNotes.plates: AG plates GO, coating it on both sides

blocks.note: Ag, the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: Someone keen to walk off with the silver plates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plates' reads as dishes; it is a verb, as silver plating coats a metal.
annotation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited.

entries.clue: Relish bluster by leader of opposition (5)

indicatorNotes.leader of: the first letter of the word after

blocks.note: a blustery wind blows in gusts

annotation.surface: Enjoying the bombast of the Leader of the Opposition.
annotation.walkthrough: The Leader of the Opposition is a real British parliamentary title, so the phrase hides a plain first-letter device.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to do something with relish or with gusto is to do it with hearty enjoyment.

entries.clue: Pit crew spoiled short race? (9)

indicatorNotes.spoiled: the letters are ruined and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A motor-racing pit crew wrecks a sprint.
annotation.walkthrough: Pit crew suggests motor racing; the pit is the orchestra pit in a theatre, and the question mark flags the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: An orchestra plays in the theatre's pit, so it is the pit's crew.

entries.clue: After finally leaving, come in again briefly with a drink (5,3)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: REENTER loses its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone leaves, pops back in for a moment and has a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After finally leaving' reads as a time phrase; it supplies the G that comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the vaguest possible word for a specific tea brewed from unfermented leaves.

entries.clue: Tossed coin with setter for earnings (6)

indicatorNotes.Tossed: the coin's letters are flipped into a new order

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as me

annotation.surface: A coin toss with the crossword setter to decide who gets the money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tossed' fits a coin perfectly, which hides that it is scrambling the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: the money coming in from work or investments.
